Features

A fishing journal built around the whole trip.

Keep the place, people, conditions, route, photos, notes, and patterns that make a day on the water worth remembering. Not just the catch.

One day.
All in one place.

Record fishing trips

Start with the day itself. Keep the date, place, notes, companions, conditions, and other details attached to one trip. Your catches, photos, locations, and route can all live inside the same record.

Log catches

Keep the fish you caught connected to the trip where they happened. Record species, time, location, photos, and the details you care about. A catch becomes more useful when you can see the day around it.

Save photos and notes

Photos are better when you remember the story around them. Keep images and journal notes with the trip instead of leaving them buried in a camera roll.

Remember the places

Save the lakes, rivers, shorelines, coves, launch points, and other places that become part of your fishing history. Over time, see where you keep returning.

Keep track of who came with you

Fishing memories are often tied to people. Keep a record of the friends, family members, and companions who shared the day.

Record conditions

Save the conditions you care about while the trip is still fresh. Later, those details can help you remember the day and recognize patterns in your own history.

Follow routes

Optional GPS tracking can preserve the path of a trip, whether you are walking, wading, paddling, trolling, or moving along a shoreline.

Build a record over time

The real value is not one entry. It is what happens after dozens, then hundreds, of days have been recorded.
